newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia still hopeful on NATO membership.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia still hopeful on NATO membership.

text.p: Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik, conceding that Slovakia might not be part of a first wave of new NATO members, has held out the prospect of joining the alliance, possibly with neutral neighbour Austria, at a later date.

"We have done everything we could, to join the first group," Hamzik said in an interview in Monday's edition of the independent daily Pravda. "If we are not in the first group, I believe we will receive the invitation (to join) later."
Slovakia is one of the post-communist countries striving to join western economic and political structures and it will hold a referendum on May 23-24 on whether to join NATO.

However, its chances of being invited to join in the first wave appear slim after repeated U.S. and European Union criticism of the pace of democratic reform. Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary are seen as front-runners.
Slovak leaders say they want to join NATO and that objections to their membership are politically motivated.
Hamzik said that if Slovakia failed to gain an invitation to join the alliance in the first round, it could still get in before the end of the century.
"There is a strong discussion on whether to join NATO in Austria," Hamzik said. "I think Austria will try to become a member of the alliance by 1999, which would create some opportunity also for us."
Hamzik said he believed Slovaks would vote in favour of NATO membership at the coming referendum.
"I assume the referendum result will be positive and therefore it will confirm our orientation," he said.

The government-sponsored referendum asks people three questions: whether they favour NATO membership, the deployment of nuclear missiles in Slovakia and the establishment of foreign military bases there.
Hamzik said he did not believe failure to join NATO could harm Slovakia's ambitions to join the European Union, calling that "irresponsible speculation".

But he added: "The question is whether the (EU) attitude towards us will be politically motivated, therefore whether our integration will be reviewed from the same point of view which dominates the (NATO) alliance's enlargement."
